data.title: UN Secretary General Guterres urges reforms of Security Council
data.description: The day began with Donald Trump threatening to annihilate Iran but ended with a three-hour meeting between US and Iranian mediators, which Trump described as “very good.” Trump also held high-level talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, with both sides saying they wanted the war in Ukraine to end before winter. Today, Zelensky and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are among those addressing the UN General Assembly, as world leaders seek ways to end the two conflicts dominating global politics. data.title: ‘I had never heard of Eswatini’: Deported by the US to a country that rejects them

data.title: Viral NATO video falsely framed as 'war propaganda' against Russia

data.title: Europe frets about Trump. But soon he could be the least of our problems | Mujtaba Rahman
data.description: The US relationship is stabilising, but how will Europe face up to Russia and China if President Le Pen is in power? I addressed a group of more than 100 European ambassadors recently on the big challenges facing the continent this year and next. My main point to these senior diplomats was that, perhaps counterintuitively, Europe’s biggest external challenges over the next 12 months will come from Russia and China, rather than the US. Europe’s relationship with Trump’s America remains difficult. The US president has weakened confidence in Nato, raised new transatlantic trade tensions and introduced uncertainty into everything from US support for Ukraine to his territorial designs on Greenland. Yet paradoxically, and notwithstanding Trump’s latest tariff threats over the EU’s outreach to Canada, the transatlantic relationship is becoming the more stable part of Europe’s external environment. Not stable, but more stable. Mujtaba Rahman is the managing director for Europe at Eurasia Group, a political risk research and consulting firm Continue reading...

data.title: ‘My body is on fire!’: my perilous, painful, perfect month of pilates
data.description: A growing number of men, including singers Shaggy and Harry Styles, are taking up pilates. When I realised I could no longer touch my toes, I decided to try it out I realised something needed to change when I nearly toppled over trying to tie my shoelaces. I was on a busy high street, with people rushing past holding shopping bags, when I saw my open shoelace spooled on the ground. I bent down to deal with it and felt gravity move against me. Only a quick flail of my arms stopped me from faceplanting. When I raised myself back upright, I felt a sharp pain in my lower back. This can’t be right, I thought. Bracing my foot on a bin to finally fix my shoelace, it dawned on me. I’d become rusty. My core strength was nonexistent, as was my flexibility. Years behind a desk had taken a toll, not helped by an after-work routine of watching TV or playing video games on the sofa. But after getting home and doing some research (yes, from my sofa), I found a potential remedy: pilates. Continue reading...

data.title: A moment that changed me: my brother gave me an unexpected gift – and a whole new life at sea
data.description: The water was my childhood playground but, as I grew up, my health left me landbound. Then my brother found a way to launch me back into the waves ... My brother and I grew up surfing at Porthcawl in south Wales. My earliest memories are of playing in the waves and I learned to bodyboard not long after I learned to walk. When I lost the use of my legs, I felt as if I had lost the sea – and a part of who I was. I was in my teens when I started to develop chronic illnesses, including endometriosis. At first, I was still able to surf – I just needed to rest afterwards. Then, in my early 20s, I developed further chronic conditions, including a connective tissue disorder that affected my joints and muscle strength. I could stand just for a few seconds and was able to walk only a few metres. At 23, an acute infection led to complications, including the loss of the use of my legs. Later, my stomach became paralysed; I’m now fed via a tube that runs down my oesophagus, through my stomach and into my intestines. Continue reading...

data.title: The Great British Bake Off review – Nigella is wise, generous … and perfect for this national treasure of a show
data.description: The newest judge on the culinary competition is a soothing presence who is the ideal complement to Paul Hollywood. Long may the show continue with her on it There’s a very good argument to be made for requiring a national referendum on whether presenters of shows that are part of our cultural identity should be allowed to leave, followed by – if necessary – a vote on who should replace them. At the very least, this would avoid the parlous state of affairs we face right now: at the very moment the public is grappling with the new-look Strictly Come Dancing (Tess and Claudia replaced by Emma Willis, Josh Widdicombe and Johannes Radebe, three whole different people!) we are asked to cope with a change to the order of the tented universe too. For The Great British Bake Off lineup has replaced Prue Leith (who stepped down after deciding that, at 86, she would quite like to go back to having holidays instead of filming the series all summer) with – the one! The only! – Nigella Lawson. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Sometimes I do cruel things – and it’s worth it’: the fabulous shameless art of the great Sophie Calle
data.description: The French artist has stalked people, posed as a hotel maid to get into rooms, and filmed her mother’s last breath. Has she any regrets? Non! As a major UK show opens, she recalls her career highs I’ve read enough interviews with Sophie Calle to know that the conversation ahead could be tricky. France’s most famous conceptual artist can be a touch evasive. Which is why I’m so surprised by the woman before me, who is friendly and seemingly open, all smiles. She’s wearing big tinted glasses, and behind them I picture her eyes twinkling. Then, 10 minutes in, she tells me she is obsessed with absence. When I ask why, she says: “Why do you live in England? Why are you wearing that sweater? I am not here to do therapy with you.” She is talking to me from the same Paris apartment she has been living in for almost 50 years. Hanging from the ceiling is a disco ball, and, alongside pictures and books, there are boxes that I imagine are filled with the innermost thoughts and feelings of her subjects. Since the early 1980s, Calle has made a name for herself with art that is at once intimate and detached, morbid and playful, immersing us in the lives of others – and in her own life, too. With a camera and a notebook in hand, she has invited strangers to sleep in her bed, posed as a hotel maid to document the belongings of guests, and called everyone in a lost address book to build a peculiarly tender portrait of its owner. Now, at 72, she is about to open her first big show in the UK for nearly two decades. Continue reading...

data.title: Huge El Niño projected to cause 450,000 deaths in next six months
data.description: New report predicts a heavy toll from Nigeria to the US – and comes on top of existing impacts of the climate crisis More than 450,000 people are projected to die from the additional heat brought by the super El Niño in the next six months, according to estimates by climate scientists. The toll is on top of the early deaths resulting from temperatures already driven up by the climate crisis. It will strike across the globe, from Indonesia to India, and Nigeria to the US. Many further deaths are expected from the droughts, wildfires and flooding that El Niños bring. Continue reading...

A network of Roman ditches containing pottery, coins, glassware and a fragment of a military helmet has been found beneath Bath Assembly Rooms in the north of the city. Continue reading...

data.title: AI looms large over Trump-Xi meeting amid deep distrust between US and China
data.description: Fears persist about Trump ‘sucking up’ to Xi on Taiwan, but few concrete outcomes anticipated from US meeting When Xi Jinping, China’s leader, touches down in Maryland on Wednesday, he will step out into the arms – perhaps a hug , if Donald Trump’s wishes come true – of a US president who has shown China more bonhomie than any of his recent predecessors. The meeting between Xi and Trump this week will be the second time that the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies have talked face to face this year. At the previous summit, held in Beijing in May, there was much talk of building a “strategic stability” between the two powers. But there was little by way of concrete outcomes : the countries remain at loggerheads over trade, export controls and geopolitics. Continue reading...

data.title: As Japan swelters, farmers turn to new heat-resistant rice varieties to boost staple crop
data.description: New rice varieties give hope that farmers can overcome the climate emergency and a warmer future that threatens harvests When schoolchildren in Shiroishi were enlisted to plant rice seedlings in June, Shinto priests blessed the land and asked the deities for a bountiful crop. Judging by the fields behind farmer Haruki Kawasaki, their prayers have been answered. The 63-year-old is preparing to harvest this year’s crop of hinatamaru , a variety of rice whose plump grains have thrived despite exposure to another hot and dry summer, conditions that typically punish rice yields. Continue reading...

Caviar and truffle flavours are on corner-shop shelves, while supermarket brands now include everything from glazed meats to blue cheese. data.title: Sali Hughes on beauty: if you can’t use retinoids, these proven anti-ageing formulas are the next best thing
data.description: Stop ‘pushing through the pain’ or ceaselessly search for the ‘right retinol’ – there are some great alternatives Anyone with an internet connection will no doubt have heard that retinoids – a group of vitamin A-based compounds – are the most evidenced and effective ingredients in treating the visible signs of skin ageing. Message received loud and clear. But what often goes unheard are the voices of many beauty consumers who have found that they simply cannot use them. All too often, I see experts online telling those complaining of discomfort, unremitting dryness, persistent redness, stinging or angry reactions that they just need to “find the right retinol” or simply “push through” the pain barrier. But I will die on this hill: not everyone can use retinoids, and they can still achieve great results without them. If I don’t convince you, believe my esteemed consultant, dermatologist Dr Justine Hextall (a woman I respect and trust so completely that I have entrusted her with my children’s skin health), because she agrees. While Hextall, as any good derm would, prescribes retinoids on a daily basis, she also sees patients for whom there is a more appropriate, kinder pathway. “While retinoids are effective, they can be difficult to tolerate and may not be used consistently in those with sensitive skin,” she says. “Consistency is the key in skincare.” Continue reading...

data.title: Another taste of honey: Shelagh Delaney’s long-lost play about a teenage truant is a little gem
data.description: The playwright’s daughter found Catch Me Who Can after her mother’s death. Now it has become a compelling audio drama with Toby Jones and Rita Tushingham Was Shelagh Delaney a one-hit wonder? Absolutely not. Aside from A Taste of Honey which, in the words of Dominic Dromgoole, “has a rock-solid heart and the gleam of the natural”, she wrote the screenplays for the films Charlie Bubbles and Dance With a Stranger, TV series including The House That Jack Built and several radio plays. But now a 30-minute piece, Catch Me Who Can , has come to light, been released as an audio drama and turns out to be a little gem. Its origins are fascinating. It deals with a teenage truant and was discovered by Delaney’s daughter, Charlotte, after her mother’s death in 2011. But why did it lay hidden for so long? According to Charlotte, who has adapted it for audio: “It imagines my last few hours on the lam having run away from home and school when I was 14 in 1978. I was gone for three days and two nights. I’d suggest it’s a racing certainty that the reason nothing has ever been heard of it is that it’s about me and my mum had rules about that kind of thing.” Continue reading...

data.title: From 50p gold hot pants to Paul Smith suits: how Kylie Minogue became one of pop’s ultimate chameleons
data.description: The star’s rise from Ramsay Street to global superstar is the subject of a new book. It’s a journey that has cleverly harnessed the power of fashion to transform, subvert – and shock On 20 December 1989, Kylie Minogue first harnessed the power of fashion. Attending the Australian premiere of her film The Delinquents, she wore a custom sequined noughts-and-crosses minidress by Australian designers Morrissey Edmiston and a cropped blond wig. She also arrived with a new accessory: a rock star boyfriend in the shape of Michael Hutchence from INXS. Before then, there’d been her Neighbours character Charlene’s peak-80s silk taffeta and lace wedding dress, and Kylie the pop star on the cover of her first album, in 1988, wearing a topless hat showing off cascading curls. But that had been fashion forced on her, at a time when she had no say in her image. Continue reading...

data.title: The Pentagon has unveiled its secret weapon: two idiotic influencers | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: Jake and Logan Paul were invited to give a motivational speech. Just don’t let them get involved with military policy We’re now approaching month seven of a war against Iran that Donald Trump repeatedly assured us would be over in a matter of weeks . Prices are rising, troop morale is plummeting , and there is little evidence things will improve. The situation is so desperate that the decision makers at the Pentagon have decided to bring out the big guns. I’m not talking about nuclear weapons, although Trump recently threatened to “blow the entire nation [of Iran] up”. No, I’m talking about influencers Jake and Logan Paul, who are famous for doing idiotic stunts on YouTube and getting hit in the face during boxing matches. Last Thursday, Pete Hegseth’s Department of Defense or whatever they’re calling it these days (the Department of War Crimes ?) welcomed the Paul brothers to Washington DC “to meet with our warriors” and deliver a motivational speech. In response, former Republican congressman and air force officer Adam Kinzinger wrote , “We aren’t a serious country at the moment.” That about sums it up. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump invades the UN with a brutish speech | Ted Widmer
data.description: Gone was any shred of US idealism. It was a spectacle of raw power – a power that is likely to only diminish in the years ahead Expectations were low for Donald Trump’s address to the UN on Tuesday, and yet somehow it was even worse than expected. He does not perform well in formal settings, like chambers of government, preferring a blingier room, like Mar-a-Lago, or an outdoor rally. For years, he has made no secret of his hostility to the UN, and the very principles of international order that define it. In recent years, that hostility has deepened into something more like a full-on assault, with frequent attacks on the international criminal court (perhaps out of fear that he will someday be indicted), on the UN’s climate agenda, and on Unesco (which the US decided to withdraw from in July 2025). Continue reading...

data.title: Great to see what Tom Cruise’s belly button looks like, but it’s the stuff he is never asked about that interests me | Marina Hyde
data.description: Most stars, and especially women, are endlessly expected to explain the past: the lessons learned and all the regrets. But not Tom – it’s Hollywood’s free pass There really is no press tour like a Tom Cruise press tour – which is why there have not really been any Tom Cruise press tours for a very long time indeed. We’re now at the stage of this one where even the interviewers have been forced on to the interview circuit to defend their interviews. Anyway: Cruise. The guy has one child with ex-wife Katie Holmes who dropped his surname as soon as she was legally allowed, and two Scientologist children widely reported to be effectively estranged from their mother, Nicole Kidman . The divorces from Kidman and Holmes were clearly deeply strange and traumatic events for both women, and have remained shrouded in unusually watertight and presumably contractual secrecy. Yet you can currently find Tom Cruise promoting his latest movie not being asked about any of this stuff, or indeed any of his other extensive “stuff” – as always – but instead doing things like giving Travis and Jason Kelce’s podcast a lecture on the benefits of VistaVision . Hate to say it, but a woman could never. Marina Hyde is a Guardian columnist. Her new book is What a Time to Be Alive! To support the Guardian, order your signed copy at guardianbookshop.com . Delivery charges may apply. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Never mind Trump – if Europe wants to save Nato, it must win over the American people | Leslie Vinjamuri
data.description: Mark Rutte has the right idea – go beyond Washington and make the case for the transatlantic alliance to the public. They may well have a willing ear At a moment when Europe is focused on persuading Donald Trump to remain committed to Nato, it needs to convince Americans, too. So the presence this evening of the Nato secretary general, Mark Rutte, in front of a public audience in Des Moines, Iowa, is significant. This is the home town of Trump’s ambassador to Nato, Matthew Whitaker, and the visit brings the debate over Nato’s future directly to a midwestern audience in a red state that operates far from elite foreign-policy circles in Washington. Rutte’s appearance is long overdue. Russia’s war in Ukraine and uncertainty over the US commitment to European security have forced European leaders to confront their dependence on Washington . While some are pressing for building European capabilities as a means to separate from the US, others see greater European defence spending as essential to keeping the US engaged. Either way, European governments can’t rely solely on meetings with Trump to secure the alliance’s future. Continue reading...

data.title: Wamser rescues point for gutsy Manchester City in WCL fightback at Bayern
data.description: Manchester City produced a gutsy performance to fight back and earn a valuable 2-2 draw away at Bayern Munich on their return to the Champions League. José Barcala’s side took the lead through Giulia Gwinn and an unfortunate Kerstin Casparij own goal but Beth Mead and Carlotta Wamser earned the visitors a hard-earned point. data.title: Great Britain exit Billie Jean King Cup after Czechia triumph in quarter-finals
data.description: Defeats for Kartal and Boulter condemn Britain to loss Men will play Germany in quarter-finals of Davis Cup Great Britain’s stay at the Billie Jean King Cup finals lasted only one match as they lost against Czechia in the quarter-finals in Shenzhen. Anne Keothavong’s side were bidding to reach the last four for the fourth time in five years but were considerable underdogs and defeats for Sonay Kartal and Katie Boulter sealed their fate. Led by the Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, the entire Czech team is ranked higher than any of Britain’s players, and it was Noskova who sealed victory with a 6-2, 7-6 (3) win against Boulter. That followed a lengthy struggle between Marie Bouzkova and Kartal lasting a minute short of three hours, which the Czech eventually won 7-6 (2), 4-6, 6-4. Continue reading...

data.title: Football Daily | Klopp, Xavi, Zidane, Mancini: big nations ready to unleash bigger dogs
data.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While Thomas Tuchel continues to gaslight his employer s at the FA into believing he was in no way responsible for England’s comically shambolic semi-final exit at the hands of Argentina, not every head coach who underperformed at the Geopolitics World Cup is still in their job. A total of 17 different managers who took teams to North America have since left their roles, with safety-first’s Steve Clarke, failing-up’s Roberto Martínez and tyranny’s Marcelo Bielsa among them. In Europe, teams such as Portugal (Jorge Jesus), Croatia (Slaven Bilic), Scotland (Sébastien Pocognoli), Czechia (Santi Denia) and Belgium (Mark van Bommel) will go into the Nations League under new management, but it is towards the bigger dogs of the football pack where Football Daily wishes to turn today’s beady gaze. Prize o’ the day to Barry Glendenning, surely, for mentioning Johnny Crumplin (football genius) in Monday’s Football Daily . As an Ipswich fan marooned in Sussex, I spent much of my teenage years at the Goldstone which, despite being a dump (I stood on the crumbling South Stand), held a certain magic for me. It still does, actually. Haven’t been to the Amex yet – hopeless nostalgia is undoubtedly a factor. The team weren’t much better than the ground for most of that time, but the 1987-88 promotion season was memorable. Garry Nelson was a bit special, Doug Rougvie had played under Fergie at Aberdeen and Gerry Armstrong had legendary status after *that* goal, but the rest of the team probably (and unfairly ) fall into the journeyman category. I loved them all. Keith Dublin dribbling his way into and then out of trouble, sleeves-up Kevin Bremner who grafted and worked the Albion into the promotion places, Deano (one of the Wilkins brothers) classy and, of course, Barry Lloyd, who never brought a sub on until the last four or five minutes, frustrating us beyond belief. And into this pantheon came teenage Johnny C who, to start with, was utterly hapless, hence the nickname football genius. Somehow, despite this, we took to him from the off and it was lovely to see how he grew into becoming an Albion legend in what were fallow years. Blimey, not sure where that all came from – you can probably tell I’m stuck out in the middle of the Fens on a slow-moving train. But thank you for bringing it all back to me!” – Jonathan Foulkes. I know the powers that be have listened to Football Daily’s ‘Stop Football’ pleas and given us very little to do for the next three weeks but, as we are just five games in to the Premier League season, can everyone stop going on about the race for the Golden Boot and which team are going to bloody champions” – Nigel Sanders. Judging by the photo of him sitting behind their ‘Life’s Good’ logo in yesterday’s Quote of the Day , LG could do a lot worse than appoint José Mourinho as a brand ambassador for their campaign. As football watchers have long known, he exudes the spirit of that exclamation from every single pore” – Andrew Parker. So, Jonathan Wilson has a new book, about football in Eastern Europe, Behind the Curtain , while his take on Zidane as the new France manager will reveal the ‘ wizard behind the curtain ’. Brilliant effort from the subeditor and marketing team working in harmony” – Paul Vickers. Continue reading...

data.title: Mikel Arteta agrees contract extension expected to keep him at Arsenal until 2030

Negotiations were put on hold during the summer transfer window but the Spaniard has reached a ­verbal agreement to extend his stay for a second time. Continue reading...

data.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings: 15 sentenced to hundreds of years in prison each over deadly terror attacks
data.description: Islamic State-inspired bombings of churches and hotels in 2019 was one of the country’s worst ever attacks A court in Sri Lanka has convicted 15 men on terrorist charges for their involvement in the deadly 2019 Easter bombings and sentenced them each to at least 220 years in prison. The terror attacks, which targeted luxury hotels and churches as they held Easter services, left 267 people dead and wounded almost 6000. The bombings, which were inspired by Islamic State (IS), were among the deadliest terror attacks in Sri Lanka’s history and sent shockwaves through the country. Continue reading...

data.title: Japan PM pledges support for international criminal court after Trump calls it ‘out of control’
data.description: Sanae Takaichi has been under domestic pressure to publicly support the ICC, after the US sanctioned the court and its Japanese president Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi , has voiced her country’s “consistent support” for the international criminal court (ICC), after Donald Trump urged member states to abandon the body, calling it “out of control”. In her speech to the UN general assembly in New York on Tuesday, Takaichi said postwar Japan had “emphasised the rule of law in the resolution of all conflicts” – a commitment she said was reflected in its support for multilateral organisations such as the ICC. data.title: Amateur archaeologist finds 934 Roman silver denarii in German field
data.description: The hoard, buried south of Cologne in the second century AD, is the biggest coin treasure ever found in Germany from the time of Hadrian An amateur archaeologist who discovered several Roman silver coins in a field in western Germany realised he had stumbled upon something much bigger when his metal detector kept beeping. Oliver Riedl called the authorities for help and a group of experts who began digging immediately discovered a total of 934 Roman silver denarii. It is the biggest coin treasure ever found in Germany from the time of the Roman emperor Hadrian, the local office in charge of archaeological monuments said on Tuesday. Continue reading...

data.title: How opencast mining risks reawakening dormant geological faults
data.description: New study finds subsidence caused by groundwater extraction can take place as far as 20km from site of mine The impact of opencast mining goes far beyond the edge of the pit. Studies of an opencast coalmine in western Germany show that opencast mining triggered extensive subsidence in the surrounding area and re-activated dormant geological faults. Underground mines are often associated with ground subsidence, but less is known about the risks associated with opencast mines. Researchers from the GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences in Potsdam, Germany, studied satellite data and geological field measurements from the area around the opencast Rhenish coalfields, between Aachen and Cologne. Continue reading...

The Trump administration said in June it was buying back the company’s US offshore wind leases for four wind projects on the east and west coasts. Continue reading...

data.title: Pay rent, eat or keep warm? Growing numbers face hard choices as housing benefit gap grows
data.description: Wirral mother among renters turning to food banks as gap between a two-bed and housing benefit hits £158 a month – rising to as much as £324 in London Do you prioritise paying the rent, putting food on the table or keeping the house warm in winter? In practice, says Laura Braddock, a single mum from Wirral, Merseyside, you always pay the rent first and improvise the rest. “If I’ve got a roof over our head, then everything else I can muddle through.” The pressing problem for Braddock, 39, is that muddling through is getting harder. The monthly rent for her two-bedroom flat far outstrips the local housing allowance (LHA) she receives – and the gap may widen. Continue reading...

data.title: Hayden Panettiere’s cause of death confirmed as fentanyl overdose
data.description: South Carolina medical examiner says ‘no signs of trauma’ and ‘the manner of death has been ruled accident’ Hayden Panettiere died from a fentanyl overdose, according to the Greenville county coroner’s office. Medical examiners in South Carolina confirmed the 36-year old actor’s cause of death on Tuesday, saying: “The cause of death has been ruled as toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol and Quetiapine.” Continue reading...

data.title: Brothers review – Woody Harrelson and Matthew McConaughey’s super-fun sitcom about the chance they’re related
data.description: The actors co-star in a lightly fictionalised meta-comedy about their real-life bromance – and possible sharing of parents. It’s a tasty little treat The cheek! The indulgence! The privilege! Did anyone, anywhere in 2026, look up from news of a world in flames and say, what we really need now is a meta-comedy where two actors play gently self-satirising fictional versions of themselves? They did not, and yet here are Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson. They once co-starred in the first season of True Detective , one of TV’s darkest and best crime dramas, but otherwise their personae have them as lifelong besties who are both free spirits, unencumbered by the rules of the fame game – not the sort of chaps who would stop and think about how their self-referential comedy bagatelle might be received. In Brothers, they portray themselves as blokes who don’t stop and think, full stop. Brothers is on Apple TV Continue reading...

data.title: North Sea, Nature Untamed review – stunning footage finds the beauty and splendour under the water
data.description: Diver Peter van Rodijnen’s footage of basking whales, plankton blooms and fatherly fish disputes the idea that the North Sea is a bleak wilderness The North Sea, with its cold grey waters, is the world’s drabbest. Or so you might have thought, but this documentary featuring the Dutch diver and underwater cinematographer Peter van Rodijnen sets out to tackle the misconceptions. His stunning footage puts all the splendours of this stormy stretch of water on show, and his voiceover gives it an endearing eccentric charm. First, the greyness. Van Rodijnen films the North Sea’s waves sparkling with the cosmic blue light of bioluminescent algae, and lit up with the disco colours of coral and plankton blooms. He also brings us cute, coo-worthy stories from the depths; take the male shorthorn sculpin fish (no looker, it must be said) who spends the winter looking after his eggs, cleaning and blowing fresh water over them. Van Rodijnen’s camera is there for the baby fish hatching – pop, pop, pop out of their pearly plump pink eggs. There are some quirky stories, too, including a barnacle with a superlong penis. Continue reading...

data.title: The Love Hypothesis review – hit BookTok romcom lacks spark on screen
data.description: Riverdale’s Lili Reinhart does some heavy lifting in Ali Hazelwood’s hit book, but it’s not quite enough Fans of the dearly departed Riverdale – or, moreover, admirers of all the batshit things the CW comic soap could make its bright young actors say with straining sincerity – have long rooted for Lili Reinhart. The Betty Cooper of yore was the best of that talented crop (Charles Melton and Camila Mendes among them) at rising above her subpar surroundings, her impressively expressive eyes able to sell the unsellable with complete conviction. She is the type of helplessly endearing performer suited to roles of naivety who masks surprise steeliness, as in her notable turn in 2019’s Hustlers or, better yet, romcoms, though there remains a dearth of worthy material. (A dual role in 2022’s Look Both Ways , a Netflix homage to Sliding Doors, didn’t cut it.) At least on paper, The Love Hypothesis, a new romcom from Amazon Prime Video, should be that material. The BookTok sensation by neuroscientist turned author Ali Hazelwood presents an ideal Reinhart protagonist: extremely nerdy, in a periodic table way, yet conventionally beautiful, awkward and self-deprecating yet cutting when it counts, the type of sweet-presenting young woman who will shout “fuck” repeatedly in private. Which Reinhart’s Olive Smith, a young biology PhD student at Stanford, winsomely does in the film’s unsettlingly cold open, as a bleary-eyed Olive, blind from expired contacts, freaking out before her grad school interview and then boldly stating her cancer-solving intentions to a brusque, handsome professor in a lab bathroom. Continue reading...

data.title: Remake review – Ross McElwee’s magnificent and moving tribute to a tragic loss and the art it inspired
data.description: Sherman’s March director McElwee revisits footage of his late son for this magnificently affecting film and meditation on making art This new film from revered documentary-maker Ross McElwee is an extraordinary work, arguably his most audacious use yet of autobiographical material while at the same time being a coruscating self-criticism of that same technique. Think of it as an artistic ouroboros (a snake eating its own tail). Remake is all at once about creativity, shame, love and loss, revelling in the way film can capture a moment of truth and honesty, but tempered by the knowledge that once a subject knows they’re being filmed everything becomes a kind of performance. It’s a film that works on so many levels and at the same time is so simple and direct. On that very simplest level, Remake starts out as a documentation of how Hollywood got in touch with McElwee and told him they wanted to make a fictionalised remake of his best-known film, Sherman’s March . Made in 1985 with a one-man crew (McElwee himself), Sherman’s March recorded the McElwee’s trip back to South Carolina where he grew up; there he films his family, old friends, and himself as he continually fails to establish romantic relationships with various women, all of it lavishly slathered with his own warm, softly southern-accented voiceover. Continue reading...

data.title: Heart of the Beast review – Brad Pitt survivalist dogmance serves up wilderness with side of cheese
data.description: Pitt and loyal hound Odin get stuck in remote Alaska in this serviceable adventure with hints of Jack London and Marley & Me One man and his dog have an amazing adventure in this survivalist drama starring Brad Pitt, from screenwriter Cameron Alexander and director David Ayer, for which the first and last words of the title have been carefully chosen to signal a mix of sentimentality and thrills. It’s an entertaining anthro-canine-mance, with man and dog relating to each other on a deep level … kind of like Owen Wilson in Marley & Me , only without Jennifer Aniston, or Bernie Winters and Schnorbitz, only without the devastating melancholy. Pitt, who last worked with Ayer on the second world war action thriller Fury , plays a US military special forces veteran called Belmont, tough, self-reliant and laconically good-humoured in the classic Pitt manner, now spending his retirement roaming the breathtaking remote landscape of Alaska in his seaplane. He is accompanied by his beloved service dog Odin, or Odey (played by four different German shepherds), who saw action with Belmont in various fuzzily imagined flashback combat sequences. Odin took retirement with Belmont and is now his best and only pal. Whether or not Belmont ever had a human partner is never revealed. Continue reading...

data.title: The Complex by Karan Mahajan review – a superb family saga set in Delhi
data.description: At once a grand sweep through history and a domestic novel of petty differences, this tale of corruption and betrayal is packed with drama We learn about the murder of the Chopra clan’s shifty, crude, charismatic patriarch Laxman in the opening pages of The Complex. Twenty-five years have passed, but the stain on this once-respectable Punjabi family remains. The man who did it, Laxman’s nephew Brij, has served his jail time and is about to be released. Some relatives think Brij is too dangerous, too shameful to return to the family home, but his son Mohit decides the pair will live together – and rewinds the clock to tell the story of the decades leading up to the crime. Karan Mahajan’s warmly received first two works, Family Planning and The Association of Small Bombs , explored individual lives alongside larger forces – urban development in the former, a car bomb’s traumatic aftermath in the latter. His excellent third novel has Delhi at its heart, but also visits Indian villages and cities, the American midwest and London, its short chapters flitting between different members of the Chopra family. You start by nodding in appreciation at Mahajan’s observant character portraits; before you know it you’re waist-deep in frustration, corruption and betrayal, as the book ranges through politics, faith, migration, infidelity and entrepreneurship. Continue reading...

data.title: Britain’s Slave Traders by William A Pettigrew review – the inconvenient truth
data.description: This revelatory history shows just how deeply embedded slavery is in the foundations of modern Britain One tedious aspect of Britain’s post-imperial melancholia is the number of amateur historians who would rather we stopped going on about our role in the slave trade. Isn’t it all in the past? Weren’t we the first to abolish it anyway? In April, the Reform party announced a new policy of halting visas to people from countries seeking slavery reparations from Britain. “The United Kingdom is not an ATM for ethnic grievances from the past,” the party’s home affairs spokesperson, Zia Yusuf, said. Unfortunately for those who would rather forget, the slave trade, as William Pettigrew argues in this grimly important book, can be found “in the depths of Britain’s grain”. Ninety per cent of the enslaved Africans transported to America went on British ships, and slave traders’ actions transformed Britain in ways that still resonate today. Continue reading...

data.title: Swan Song by Charles Spencer review – a furious exercise in score-settling by Diana’s brother
data.description: Amid genuinely touching passages about his sister, the earl can’t help but put himself and his grievances centre stage Charles Spencer’s Swan Song, a memoir of his relationship with his sister, the late Diana, Princess of Wales, is a fascinating document that tells us a little about Diana and a great deal about Charles Spencer – perhaps more than we needed to know. If that sounds snarky, after 400 pages of score settling, chest thumping, wild indiscretion and some truly touching passages about his late sister, the reader is left with a head-spinning story of the world that created Diana and a certain sourness at the manner in which it is told. Let’s start with the headlines in last week’s Daily Mail, the newspaper to whom Spencer sold serialisation of a book which includes a line describing tabloid journalists as “those who inhabit the murky swamps of malevolence, and who need to suck their victims dry of their souls”. Perhaps he meant a different set of hacks. Anyway the top line in the Mail was that, shortly after Diana’s death, King Charles insulted her in a phone call to Spencer: “‘Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough.’” Your take on this quote will likely dictate how you receive the book, and here’s mine: I’m willing to believe the king behaved badly, but “hissed” is a red flag, one of those embellishments, like “snarled” or “flounced”, that writers tend to use to make those they’re writing about appear worse. Spencer, always the injured party, has so many axes grinding away in this book that at times it’s impossible to hear what he’s saying. Continue reading...

data.title: Catarina and the Beauty of Killing Fascists review – It caused fury across Europe. In the UK? Laughter and coughing
data.description: National Theatre, London Tiago Rodrigues’s play has incensed audiences abroad with one character’s hellfire rightwing invective. But its combination of boredom and shocks ultimately feels confusing What does it say about an audience who, while watching a character make a speech that has sparked screeching protests and angry walkouts in its run across Europe, sit politely listening until the end? The booing does come, but only after the actor playing a far-right politician and kidnap victim (Romeu Costa) has finished a half-hour invective that takes in everything from the scourge of minorities to that of elites, homosexuals, and the far-left. It is a masterclass in rightwing rabble-rousing, with its appropriation of the word “freedom”. Yet on press night at its British premiere, all that is summoned in response is nervous laughter, a chorus of coughs and a few loud whistles. Continue reading...

data.title: Previous winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart shortlisted for Booker prize
data.description: The two authors are in the running for the £50,000 award alongside a Pulitzer winner, a science fiction legend, a comic writer and a debut novelist • Booker judge Mary Beard on this year’s shortlist This year’s Booker prize shortlist features some very familiar names – previous winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart are in the running once more, along with Pulitzer winner Elizabeth Strout and prominent British speculative fiction writer M John Harrison. Novelist and poet Luke Kennard and debut novelist Rebecca Perry are also in contention for the £50,000 prize, the winner of which will be announced on Monday 9 November. James, the Jamaican writer who took home the prize in 2015 for A Brief History of Seven Killings, was shortlisted this time for The Disappearers . Set in Aids-era Jamaica, the novel centres around an attack on a group of queer men rehearsing John Herbert’s prison-set play Fortune and Men’s Eyes. Coming in at 640 pages, it’s the longest on the list. Continue reading...

data.title: Can a ballerina do a stomp? Natalia Osipova on making her fearsome, foul-mouthed acting debut
data.description: Osipova plays the wife of bisexual economist John Maynard Keynes in a new play. The ballerina talks about the allure of her Russian character, dismissed as a ‘frivolous foghorn of a chorus girl’ When Natalia Osipova started rehearsals for her first ever play, it didn’t go well. “I cry. I’m shaking. I’m stressed and completely lost on the first day,” she reports. “I think, ‘I’m a piece of shit!’ I want to take a taxi and run away.” It’s the second week of rehearsals when we meet, and Osipova is still here. The Royal Ballet principal plays a Russian ballerina from a previous age: Lydia Lopokova , who danced with Diaghilev’s Ballets Russes, then in 1925 unexpectedly married British economist John Maynard Keynes, who is the protagonist of James Graham’s The Standard of Living – a play about, among other things, taking risks and imagining a brave new future. Acting is central to ballet’s appeal for Osipova. “Maybe I’ll never be super perfect for classical ballet because I love stories so much,” she says. Even so, she demurred when former colleague Edward Watson suggested she audition. “You’re stupid!” was his retort. “You need to try because it’s amazing opportunity.” A delicate silver necklace shines beneath frank brown eyes. Osipova requested a translator in our previous interviews, but today speaks in an idiosyncratic gallop not unlike Lopokova’s own. Entering Nicholas Hytner’s rehearsal room, joining a classy cast led by Rory Kinnear, she felt like Lydia among Keynes’s sneery Bloomsbury friends. “I left rehearsal and cried,” she says, “because I feel, ‘Oh my god, I’m so bad.’ But you learn and listen and every day, step by step, I do better.” Continue reading...

data.title: The amazing life of 101-year-old art warrior Ce Roser: ‘We made noise. We closed the streets’
data.description: Sick of her friends getting nowhere, she co-founded The Women in the Arts Foundation and they protested across New York. Ahead of a UK show, Roser talks about escaping wartime Shanghai – and still painting three a day In January of 1971, the American art historian Linda Nochlin published a landmark essay, Why Have There Been No Great Women Artists? It was a provocation and a call to arms that was to send shockwaves through the arts establishment. “It wasn’t just a problem for artists,” says Ce Roser, more than half a century on. “My older friends could not get shows, although they had had brilliant careers before, and that happened also to all of my friends who were poets or writers. Nobody seemed to be able to establish themselves as career artists. So we got together, we complained, and I decided we should have a meeting and really talk seriously about it.” Continue reading...

data.title: The great iced coffee debate: is it wrong to take a beverage into a job interview?
data.description: It might seem a perfectly natural thing to do. data.title: The secret to making jackfruit curry that actually tastes of something | Kitchen aide
data.description: Jackfruit is a blank canvas that absorbs flavour brilliantly – it’s all about seasoning it generously and giving it enough time for the aromatics and spices to do their work I’ve just made yet another disappointing jackfruit curry . Any tips for making it more flavourful? Sally, by email “The trick with jackfruit is not to rush it,” says Eroshan Meewella, founder of Sri Lankan street-food joint Adoh! in central London. “It absorbs flavour brilliantly – spice, curry leaves, coconut milk, tamarind – so you just need to give it time.” Don’t be shy with those flavours, either, because, as Sally has discovered, jackfruit is something of a blank canvas. Sanjana Modha, author of Modern Masala , suggests treating it a bit as you would tofu: “You really have to build flavour around it. Think of jackfruit as a sponge that’s going to absorb your masala. And I cannot emphasise enough how you’ll need more onions than you think.” And she ain’t kidding: for a curry to feed four to six, Modha uses “at least” four large onions. “You must spend time caramelising them properly, so start by getting those onions really golden by frying them with a couple of cinnamon sticks, cloves and cardamom pods.” That will take a good 45 minutes. “Then add ginger, garlic and chillies – don’t be afraid to season generously with all your ground spices.” You’ll want some acidity, too: “Lemon, lime or tamarind towards the end to balance everything.” On to the jackfruit itself, which Luke Larsson, head chef at Khao Bird in London, always uses fresh from an Asian supermarket: “It’s just a hundred times better [than tinned], and it’s such a delicious fruit when fresh.” Modha, meanwhile, tends to go for tinned young green jackfruit in brine: “Drain and rinse it really well, then pat it completely dry using kitchen towel.” She fries it first in neutral oil (rapeseed, sunflower), until golden and slightly caramelised: “This gives it much more flavour, then I marinate it in ground spices and a spoonful of mustard oil for a few hours, or even overnight, before adding it to my curry.” Got a culinary dilemma? Email feast@theguardian.com Continue reading...

data.title: Country diary: An autumn bounty of fruits is well on its way | John Gilbey
data.description: Cardigan: Taking a walk beside the River Teifi, I encounter trees beginning to fade into new season colour, and the low blur of a weasel It is rare for me to visit the same place twice within a couple of weeks, but my walk in the Teifi Marshes recently was curtailed by heavy rain, and I feel that I have unfinished business. Last time I started from the Cilgerran end of the marsh, so today begin at the seaward side – crossing the bridge over the Teifi and heading upstream past the site of the old, sadly long-departed Cardigan railway station . My route follows the former course of the railway line, but I briefly divert along a boardwalk into the broad reedbeds at the heart of the marsh. Here, I am surrounded by the ambient sound of the wind in the reeds, which ebbs and flows with an almost animate organic static – pushing back the distant sounds of traffic on the main road. Scrub and small trees interact with the reeds at the margins, their autumn bounty of fruits already well advanced. The blackberries are almost over, but the sloes are plump and mature with the promise of a warming winter spirit to come. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The choice was prison or exile’: journalists who fled Russia publish grim portrait of Putin
data.description: Roman Badanin and Mikhail Rubin, who were forced to move abroad in 2021, tell of president capable of ‘limitless cruelty’ At 6am on 29 June 2021, the Russian journalist Roman Badanin was woken by a knock on the door of his family’s Moscow apartment. “Come quickly, someone has scratched your car in the courtyard,” a voice shouted from outside. As he opened the door, masked men pushed their way in. Across the city, a similar raid was happening at the home of Badanin’s colleague Mikhail Rubin. The masked men were officers of the FSB , the Russian intelligence service, instruments of the “climate of fear and violence” that the journalists say Vladimir Putin has imposed on Russia in their forensically detailed biography of the Russian president. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I’m afraid they’ll bomb the cafe where I work, or bomb me’: a day in the life of a 12-year-old boy in Gaza
data.description: This week, as the war in Gaza approaches its fourth year, the Guardian follows five ordinary Palestinians as they go about their lives. Each tells the story of their day, revealing the terrible toll of the conflict. Ramadan lives in a tent on the beach and works to support his family As the war in Gaza approaches its fourth year, this week, the Guardian follows five ordinary Palestinians as they go about their lives. Each will tell the story of their day, revealing the terrible toll of the ongoing conflict. The tent is pitched on a platform set in the sloping sand dunes, above a long expanse of golden coastline. Rats have chewed holes in its canvas sides, and tendrils of pale sand blow in through the gaps. Inside, on the torn mattress he shares with his siblings, 12-year-old Ramadan Ghaban blinks the sleep from his eyes. The sun has just risen but it is already hot. I wake up every morning at 6 .30am. Sometimes, the heat wakes me up, and sometimes it is the sound of the birds, which are everywhere because we live near the sea. Continue reading...

data.title: In 2021, researchers began placing concrete-block oyster reefs on Prince Edward Island; biomass rose 45-fold
data.description: Innovative artificial oyster reefs have been created off Prince Edward Island to boost marine biodiversity and create habitats. In just two years, these structures attracted 45 different species, enhancing biomass significantly. They also offered vital surfaces for oyster growth, improving environmental conditions. The initiative, in collaboration with Lennox Island First Nation, highlights the ecological and cultural significance of restoring oyster populations and demonstrates new methods for revitalizing coastal ecosystems.

data.title: Tasmania removed invasive rice grass; fish species more than doubled in 3 years
data.description: Tasmania’s Duck Bay wetland is showing signs of recovery after years of work to remove invasive rice grass. Circular Head Landcare has reduced the weed from about 50 hectares to five, allowing native saltmarsh plants to return. University of Tasmania scientists found fish species increased from five to 11, with yellow-eye mullet and other species returning to restored areas.

data.title: Nova técnica pode desobstruir artérias calcificadas sem uso de stent
data.description: A calcificação das artérias coronárias é um dos indicadores de maior risco quando se trata da saúde do coração . Estima-se que a associação do cálcio com o acúmulo de gordura ao longo dos anos ocorra em nove de cada 10 pacientes com aterosclerose . Ainda que não tenha sintomas aparentes, esse processo obstrui os vasos, tornando-os mais rígidos, e aumentacmuito o risco de complicações como o infarto . Leia mais (09/22/2026 - 20h42)

data.title: Ingmar Nevéus: Därför skjuter Trump upp ”stora beslutet” om Iran
data.description: NEW YORK. Donald Trump har ”ett stort beslut att fatta” om Iran, sade han i sitt tal till FN:s generalförsamling. Ska USA ”driva landet till helvetet” – eller göra upp med regimen i Teheran? Så har han sagt förut, utan att få slut på kriget. Det nya för dagen är att det stora beslutet skjuts upp till efter kongressvalet i november.

data.title: Dit jaar veel meer paarden met westnijlvirus, en de symptomen zijn ernstig. 'Sommige paarden overlijden, andere moeten met euthanasie uit hun lijden worden verlost'
data.description: In Nederland werd dit jaar al bij 88 paarden een besmetting met het westnijlvirus vastgesteld – het topje van de ijsberg, volgens experts. De dieren kunnen ernstige neurologische verschijnselen krijgen. Vaccinatie verkleint het risico daarop, maar de dierenarts waarschuwt: dure en trage testen laten „soms wel drie weken” op zich wachten, wat de meldingsbereidheid ondermijnt.

data.title: Ten dom ma zaledwie 14 m² i jest samowystarczalny. Architekt sprytnie ukrył łóżko
data.description: Co można zmieścić w domu, którego powierzchnia użytkowa ma mniej niż 15 mkw.? Okazuje się, że całkiem sporo. Na Słowacji, nad zamkiem Devín i na skraju winnic Zlatý Roh, powstała bardzo nietypowa inwestycja. Ten niewielki domek jest samowystarczalny i przeznaczony do całorocznego użytkowania.

data.title: Proč nenávidíte mladé lidi a chcete jim zničit budoucnost? řekl Hřib Okamurovi
data.description: Změnu zákona, která zastaví pravidelné zdražování dálničních známek, právě schvalují poslanci. Vládní návrh ruší každoroční valorizaci jejich cen. Za roční známku tak motoristé zaplatí i v dalších letech 2570 korun, za měsíční 480 korun, za desetidenní 300 korun a za jednodenní 230 korun. Zůstanou úlevy pro vozidla s alternativním pohonem.

data.title: Podzim se odkládá. Babí léto začne o víkendu a protáhne se do října
data.description: Ač uplynulý týden do Česka po období nadprůměrných teplot vrátil typické počasí pro polovinu září – tedy chladné noci a maxima pod dvaceti stupni Celsia – meteorologové upozorňují na blížící se opětovné oteplení. Babí léto dle výhledu přijde o nadcházejícím prodlouženém víkendu. ČHMÚ navíc uvádí, že nadprůměrné teploty nějakou dobu vydrží.

data.title: Probrala jsem se a znásilňoval mě. Tvář toxické maskulinity čelí obvinění
data.description: Streamer Clavicular, jedna z hlavních tváří takzvané manosféry, čelí obvinění ze znásilnění dívky, které v té době bylo sedmnáct let. Údajně ji opil a zdrogoval. Streamer obvinění odmítá a naznačuje, že z něj dívka chce jen vydolovat peníze.

data.title: Deset miliard na pokutách za 35 let existence. Antimonopolní úřad slaví výročí
data.description: Úřad pro ochranu hospodářské soutěže (ÚOHS) ve středu oslavil výročí 35 let od svého vzniku. Za tu dobu provedl přes 3100 řízení a uložil pokuty za více než deset miliard korun, uvedl na konferenci jeho předseda Petr Mlsna. Úřad podle něj v brzké době chystá vydání dalšího kartelového rozhodnutí, které celkovou částku pokut ještě výrazně zvýší.

data.title: Nejdražší ministryně, ptá se Jurečka na škrty dávek nezaměstnaným Schillerové
data.description: Exministra práce a sociálních věcí, šéfa lidoveckých poslanců Mariana Jurečka zajímá, proč chce ANO škrtnout reformu ve vyplácení dávek v nezaměstnanosti, pro kterou přitom s předchozí vládní koalicí Petra Fialy hlasovalo. „Drahá, nejdražší ministryně financí,“ oslovil ministryni Alenu Schillerovou. „Jdete proti vlastním lidem,“ prohlásil ve středu ve Sněmovně Jurečka.

data.title: Drama v Kadani. Cizinci vytáhli pistoli na dva muže, hrozili pomocí překladače
data.description: Dva cizinci vytáhli na veřejném místě v Kadani na Chomutovsku na dva jiné muže zbraň a vyhrožovali jim smrtí, pokud útočníkům neobstarají drogy. Jednalo se o plynovou pistoli, ze které agresoři dvakrát vystřelili, když se poškození pokusili utéct. Pachatele nakonec zadrželi svědci. Kriminalisté už je obvinili.

data.title: Vědci v Brně testují lepidlo na kosti, inspirovali se mušlemi. Samo se vstřebá
data.description: S léčbou tříštivých zlomenin může v budoucnu pomoci kostní lepidlo, které testují vědci z výzkumného centra CEITEC Vysokého učení technického v Brně. Jednotlivé úlomky lze přilepit na své místo, poté se lepidlo postupně vstřebá a rozloží na látky, které se v těle běžně vyskytují. Vědci momentálně řeší také patentování vynálezu.

data.description: Pouhých pět subjektů se zúčastní komunálních voleb v třicetitisícovém Trutnově. Je to zdaleka nejméně od roku 1990. Občanská demokratická strana, která volby v okresním městě vyhrává od roku 1994, se spojila s TOP 09 a KDU-ČSL. Volební koalici sestavily PRO a SPD.

data.title: Pražská plynárenská a E.ON zdražují
data.description: Firmy E.ON a Pražská plynárenská v minulých dnech zdražily některé své fixované produkty elektřiny a plynu. Zvýšení cen většinou v řádu stovek korun za megawatthodinu (MWh) se týká nových zákazníků. Firmy reagují na současný růst cen energií na velkoobchodním trhu. Dodávky energií v důsledku blízkovýchodní krize v minulých měsících zdražovali i další dodavatelé.

data.title: Když se Havel a underground potkali u soudu. Před 50 lety začala rašit Charta 77
data.description: Před padesáti lety začalo na chodbách soudu v Karmelitské ulici v Praze vznikat jedno z nejsilnějších hnutí proti totalitnímu komunistickému režimu, Charta 77. Osobnosti, které do té doby nemohly najít společnou řeč, se spojily, aby tak pomohly undergroundu. Tedy mládeži, která poslouchala rockovou hudbu a chtěla žít po svém.

data.title: Oneplay Sport rozšiřuje hokejovou nabídku. Na obrazovky míří Univerzitní liga
data.description: Oneplay Sport rozšiřuje hokejovou nabídku o Univerzitní ligu ledního hokeje. V sezoně 2026/2027 odvysílá 28 přímých přenosů, první je na programu 8. října. Stanice tak chce oslovit mladší generaci diváků. Součástí vysílání proto nebude jen zápas, ale reportéři budou přibližovat dění na stadionech, atmosféru na tribunách, rivalitu škol i příběhy studentů, kteří kombinují hokej s vysokoškolským studiem.

data.title: Prostějov řeší před volbami hlavně nedostupné bydlení a chybějící parkovací místa
data.description: Minulé komunální volby v Prostějově jasně vyhrálo hnutí ANO v čele s Františkem Jurou a následně vytvořilo koalici s ODS a Pévéčkem, která disponovala pohodlnou většinou 22 hlasů. Primátorem tak zůstal Jura, jenž by post rád znovu obhájil. Po čtyřech letech se teď mezi hlavní témata voleb řadí evergreen v podobě dopravy a parkování, dále dostupné bydlení či velké městské investice.

data.title: Rychlobruslařská hala na okraji Českých Budějovic? Jihočeský kraj nabídl prostor
data.description: Sportovní areál a tréninkové centrum na Složišti v Českých Budějovicích roky slouží především pro fotbalisty. Jihočeský kraj před časem získal rozsáhlé pozemky blízko sjezdu z dálnice D3 od města a hned oznámil, že ho chce dál rozvíjet. Hejtman Marin Kuba v úterý sdělil, že už informoval premiéra i ministra sportu o tom, že by tam mohla vzniknout i první rychlobruslařská hala v České republice. Premiér Babiš potvrdil, že jsou ve hře dvě místa: Žďár nad Sázavou a Budějovice.

data.title: Nastal astronomický podzim. Rovnodennost nastala v noci, letní čas skončí až za měsíc
data.description: Na severní polokouli začal astronomický podzim. Slunce pomyslně překročilo rovník a nastala podzimní rovnodennost, kdy jsou den a noc přibližně stejně dlouhé. Léto však ještě zcela nekončí. Na víkend meteorologové slibují počasí s 25 stupni a letní čas skončí až na konci října.

data.title: „Ukončete válku.“ Šéf íránské diplomacie sdělil podmínky pro Hormuzský průliv
data.description: Íránský ministr zahraničí Abbás Arakčí se v New Yorku na okraj zasedání Valného shromáždění OSN osobně setkal se zvláštním americkým zmocněncem Stevem Witkoffem. Sdělil mu „striktní“ podmínky Teheránu pro znovuotevření Hormuzského průlivu. Země požaduje okamžité zrušení americké blokády íránských přístavů, uvolnění zmrazených íránských aktiv a ukončení války na všech frontách „odporu“.

data.description: Každý začínající realitní makléř by si měl pečlivě prostudovat, jak Donald Trump sháněl grónskou parcelu. Za prvé, aby si uvědomil, že hodnota nemovitostí může v čase divoce skákat. data.title: Začala nová energetická krize, jiná než poslední. Jak sáhne do našich peněženek?
data.description: Zatímco předcházející energetická krize byla pro Evropskou unii náhlým strukturálním šokem spojeným s dramatickým omezením, ba až zastavením dodávek ruského potrubního plynu do EU, nyní je situace jiná. Nejde o náhlou ztrátu hlavního dodavatele, ale o geopolitické napětí mj. na Blízkém východě dopadající na námořní trasy a zvýšenou citlivost trhu na sezonní výkyvy či stav zásobníků plynu.

data.title: PCP leva a debate início do ano letivo e aponta a Governo "fragilizado"
data.description: Convicto de que são “necessárias respostas para a resolução dos problemas da escola pública”, o PCP agendou para esta quarta-feira um debate de atualidade no Parlamento sobre o início do ano letivo. O ministro da Educação vai representar o Governo na Assembleia da República, confirmou a RTP Antena 1, juntamente com o Secretário de Estado Adjunto e da Educação, Alexandre Homem Cristo, e a Secretária de Estado da Administração Escolar, Maria Luísa Oliveira.

data.title: All-rounder Jacks stars as England beat Sri Lanka in 1st ODI

His quickfire 46 not out helped guide England to a competitive 265 all out after they lost momentum following the exit of captain Harry Brook for 67. data.title: Bénin : une première cargaison de pétrole brut attendue sur le marché international en octobre
data.description: © La Nation Bénin La première cargaison de pétrole brut béninois, estimée à 250.000 barils, sera mise sur le marché international en octobre prochain, a annoncé mardi le quotidien béninois de service public La Nation. Selon le journal, le projet est piloté par Akrake Petroleum Benin, filiale du groupe singapourien Rex International Holding et opérateur du bloc 1, qui abrite le gisement de Sèmè, dans le sud-est du pays. "Pour ce début, la production journalière est d'une taille modeste, environ 3.000 barils par jour. Ce qui pourrait progressivement atteindre 5.000, voire 6.000 barils selon les attentes de la société", a rapporté La Nation. Le journal a rappelé qu'en mars 1984, la Banque mondiale avait publié un document révélant qu'en 1968, la compagnie américaine Union Oil Company of California avait identifié un gisement offshore dans les eaux bordant Sèmè. "Ainsi avaient démarré les recherches géologiques qui ont inscrit le pays sur la liste des territoires prospectés pour des ressources pétrolières. Plusieurs autres études vont suivre des années durant avec diverses organisations et structures spécialisées dans l'exploration et l'exploitation pétrolière. Des accords vont être signés, les recherches intensifiées avec de nouvelles technologies", explique l'article. D'après La Nation, le projet est finalement entré dans sa phase opérationnelle en août 2025, avec le déploiement par Akrake Petroleum d'équipements lourds sur le bloc 1. "Au début de l'année, cet opérateur annonce le succès du forage du puits qui s'étend sur 1.405 mètres à l'horizontal, dont 950 mètres traversent une formation pétrolifère sans présence d'eau, indiquant un réservoir exploitable d'une production initiale de 15.000 barils par jour, selon le rapport opérationnel publié par l'entreprise", peut-on lire dans l'article. Cet article Bénin : une première cargaison de pétrole brut attendue sur le marché international en octobre est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Conférence One Health à Rome : le Cameroun plaide pour des normes au service du terrain
data.description: © DR Représentant le Cameroun à la Conférence Mondiale sur l'approche « Une seule santé » organisée par la FAO à Rome, le Ministre de l'Élevage, Dr Taïga, a délivré un message fort : les normes internationales n'ont de valeur que si elles sont appliquées concrètement. Il a présenté le modèle camerounais, entre architecture institutionnelle et capacités opérationnelles. Le Cameroun fait entendre sa voix à Rome.A l'occasion de la Conférence Mondiale sur l'Application de l'Approche « Une seule santé » dans les systèmes agroalimentaires, organisée par la FAO, le Ministre de l'Élevage, des Pêches et des Industries Animales, Dr Taïga, a plaidé pour des normes internationales au service du terrain. Devant les hauts responsables de la FAO, ministres et ambassadeurs, il a rappelé l'interdépendance entre santés humaine, animale, végétale et environnementale. « Le Codex Alimentarius, les normes de l'OMSA, les normes phytosanitaires et le Règlement Sanitaire International fournissent un langage commun pour gérer les risques », a-t-il souligné. Situé au cœur du bassin du Congo, le Cameroun est exposé aux risques zoonotiques. Les épisodes d'anthrax et la mortalité des grands singes dans la Réserve du Dja en 2005 ont conduit à la création d'une Stratégie nationale, devenue aujourd'hui le Programme National de Lutte contre les Zoonoses (PNPLZER), plateforme « One Health » placée sous la supervision des Services du Premier Ministre. Une dynamique soutenue par l'ANOR avec plus de 3 200 normes référencées, dont 113 homologuées en élevage en 2024 et 25 en technologie alimentaire en 2025, et sur le terrain par le LANAVET, le RESCAM et le Centre d'urgence en santé animale. Le Dr Taïga a dégagé trois leçons : adapter les normes sans perdre leur cohérence, exiger un portage politique au plus haut niveau, et bâtir des capacités opérationnelles concrètes. Cet article Conférence One Health à Rome : le Cameroun plaide pour des normes au service du terrain est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Le Yango Fellowship réunit des talents technologiques de six pays africains pour développer des solutions ancrées dans les réalités locales
data.description: © YANGO Des boursiers de Côte d’Ivoire, du Ghana, de Zambie, du Sénégal, d’Éthiopie et du Mozambique présentent des projets technologiques répondant à des enjeux liés au transport, à la santé, à la finance, à l’emploi, à la gestion des déchets et à l’accès à l’eau en Afrique Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire – 21 septembre 2026 : Yango Group a clôturé l’édition 2026 du Yango Fellowship panafricain à l’occasion d’une cérémonie de remise des diplômes et d’un Pitch Day organisés sur deux jours à Abidjan. L’événement a réuni 24 boursiers issus de six pays africains, venus présenter les projets technologiques qu’ils ont développés tout au long du programme. La cohorte réunissait des boursiers de Côte d’Ivoire, du Ghana, de Zambie, du Sénégal, d’Éthiopie et du Mozambique, sélectionnés parmi plus de 600 candidats. Au cours des 12 semaines du programme, les boursiers ont travaillé au sein de six équipes composées de participants de différents pays, passant de la définition des problématiques et de la recherche à la conception de solutions, à l’élaboration de modèles économiques, au prototypage et à la présentation finale de leurs projets. Les solutions développées couvrent notamment les paiements sans espèces dans le transport informel, l’identité financière numérique pour les commerçants du secteur informel, la visibilité sur l’approvisionnement en médicaments pour les agents de santé communautaires, la mise en relation transfrontalière entre candidats et employeurs, la collecte intelligente et le recyclage des déchets, ainsi que des solutions à faible coût pour tester la qualité de l’eau dans les communautés rurales. La cérémonie de clôture à Abidjan a combiné le développement des projets avec des échanges auprès de leaders du secteur technologique et du monde des affaires. Les fellows ont participé à une session consacrée à l’IA au service de l’impact, animée par Celina Lee, cofondatrice de Zindi, ainsi qu’à des ateliers pratiques de prise de parole en public et de préparation au pitch. Ils ont également rencontré des dirigeants de Yango Group issus de plusieurs marchés africains afin d’échanger sur l’évolution professionnelle, l’entrepreneuriat et la création d’entreprises technologiques adaptées aux différents contextes locaux. Lors du Pitch Day final, les boursiers ont présenté six projets collectifs ainsi qu’une sélection de projets individuels devant un jury composé d’experts des secteurs de la technologie, de l’investissement et de l’industrie. L’événement s’est conclu par une cérémonie de remise de prix, avec une dotation totale de 12 000 USD destinée à récompenser les meilleurs projets collectifs et individuels. Africoded a remporté le premier prix dans la catégorie des projets collectifs, d’une valeur de 4 500 USD , pour sa plateforme assistée par l’intelligence artificielle qui met en relation les demandeurs d’emploi africains avec des opportunités professionnelles transfrontalières, des emplois à distance et des possibilités de développement de carrière à travers le continent. Harambee s’est classé deuxième et a reçu 2 500 USD pour sa plateforme intelligente de collecte et de recyclage des déchets reliant les ménages, les collecteurs et les acteurs du recyclage. Bloom a remporté la troisième place ainsi qu’un prix de 1 500 USD pour son projet African Transit Payment Revolution , un système de paiement sans espèces conçu pour les transports publics informels en Afrique de l’Est et de l’Ouest. Dans la catégorie individuelle, Fredrick Mwepu , de Zambie, a remporté le prix du Meilleur projet individuel , doté de 1 500 USD , pour RoboCore Zambia , une plateforme de robotique développée localement afin de rendre l’enseignement pratique des STEM plus accessible et plus abordable. Le Ghanéen Meshack Kwame Nartey a reçu le deuxième prix, d’un montant de 1 000 USD , pour Shuttle Smart Ghana , une application permettant de suivre les navettes universitaires et de fournir aux étudiants des informations en temps réel sur leur arrivée. Oulimata Rose Dia a reçu le prix de la Meilleure contribution technique/IA , doté de 1 000 USD , pour Smart Bin Collection , un système alimenté à l’énergie solaire qui surveille en temps réel le niveau de remplissage des poubelles et utilise la connectivité 2G afin d’optimiser la collecte des déchets. « 600 candidatures pour 24 places ne signifient pas que l’Afrique manque de talents ; elles montrent au contraire combien de talents attendent encore un accès structuré au mentorat et aux opportunités. L’Afrique ne manque pas de jeunes brillants. Ce qui est plus difficile à trouver, c’est un mentor, un réseau et la possibilité de confronter une idée à un problème réel. C’est précisément ce manque que le Fellowship cherche à combler », a déclaré Shashi Singh, Directeur des opérations, Yango Ride MEA & Asie . « Les outils pratiques dédiés aux STEM étaient quelque chose que je ne voyais autrefois que dans des vidéos. RoboCore Zambia existe pour combler ce manque, afin que le prochain étudiant qui souhaite construire quelque chose n’ait pas à attendre l’opportunité que j’ai moi-même failli ne jamais avoir. Je suis très heureux que mon projet ait pu voir le jour. Ce fut une expérience formidable de voyager, de rencontrer d’autres boursiers venus de différents pays et d’apprendre directement auprès d’experts et de leaders des secteurs de la technologie et de l’IA. C’est une expérience que je n’oublierai jamais », a déclaré Fredrick Mwepu , étudiant zambien en STEM et lauréat du prix du Meilleur projet individuel pour RoboCore Zambia, sa plateforme de robotique développée localement afin de rendre l’enseignement pratique des STEM plus accessible et plus abordable. Le programme répond à une réalité plus large à l’échelle du continent : la croissance numérique repose sur les personnes, et pas uniquement sur les infrastructures. Développer et faire évoluer des technologies localement nécessite des ingénieurs, des entrepreneurs et des professionnels de la technologie disposant d’une expérience pratique, mais aussi des personnes qui comprennent les réalités propres à leurs marchés. Pour Yango Group, investir dans ces talents est étroitement lié à la manière dont l’entreprise se développe en Afrique : les infrastructures, les comportements et les besoins diffèrent d’un marché à l’autre, et la construction d’entreprises locales solides nécessite donc une expertise locale forte. Le Fellowship constitue l’une des initiatives à travers lesquelles Yango contribue à renforcer ce vivier de talents tout en créant des liens au sein de l’écosystème technologique africain au sens large. À propos de Yango Group Yango Group est une entreprise technologique internationale qui transforme des technologies développées à l’échelle mondiale en services du quotidien adaptés aux communautés locales. Portés par un engagement constant en faveur de l’innovation, nous repensons et améliorons des technologies de pointe issues du monde entier afin de les intégrer de manière fluide dans des services quotidiens adaptés aux besoins de différentes régions. Yango Group propose ses services numériques, notamment dans les domaines de la mobilité, de la livraison, de la foodtech et du divertissement, entre autres, dans plus de 30 pays en Afrique, en Amérique latine, en Europe, au Moyen-Orient, en Asie du Sud et dans d’autres régions.
